articles.why_it_matters: The key milestone is booting actual GTA VI code, not just translating shaders. A developer repository can be active long before the game runs.
articles.verification: Developer self-report, not independent gameplay verification
articles.description: Leonida claims all 26,503 RDNA2 shaders translated but says GTA VI does not boot yet.

articles.title: VX Underground examined alleged GTA VI assets; this is not an executable safety test
articles.summary: PC Gamer reports that cybersecurity researchers at VX Underground reviewed files in the alleged Xbox game-data dump and considered the assets genuine. That is a reported assessment of the data archive, not a malware assessment of Cyberleek's promised November 23 executable.
articles.why_it_matters: A claim that asset files look genuine does not establish the safety of a separate executable, and it does not prove GTA VI can be played on Windows. Any future security claim needs the exact file hash and independently reviewed behavior.
articles.verification: PC Gamer attribution of VX Underground's initial examination. No independent clearance of the promised executable is established.

articles.title: Cyberleek's November 23 executable promise: what is actually verified?
articles.summary: Decrypt reports Cyberleek's claim that it shared a roughly 209 GB Xbox build while withholding its executable. The group says it will release that missing file on November 23 regardless of whether a $15 million memecoin target is met. Independent verification of the files is still absent.
articles.why_it_matters: Even a genuine executable would not automatically make GTA VI playable on Windows: Leonida and Xbox emulation still require extensive runtime compatibility. A crypto fundraising claim is not evidence of a working port.
articles.verification: November 21 reporting on an unverified claim. No independently confirmed PC boot or authenticated executable.

articles.title: GTA VI has officially launched on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S
articles.summary: Take-Two and Rockstar announced that GTA VI became available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19. The original release announcement lists the console editions, not a Windows launch.
articles.why_it_matters: This is the official platform baseline. Separate it from PC release predictions and third-party port experiments.
articles.verification: Original Take-Two investor-relations release, November 19, 2026.

articles.title: How Rockstar scales GTA VI: 720p Series S, 1440p PS5/Series X, PSSR on Pro
articles.summary: VGC quotes Rockstar developers explaining the console rendering pipeline: Xbox Series S starts from 720p and uses AMD FSR Upscaling 4 toward 1080p, while PS5 and Series X upscale a 1440p base and PS5 Pro uses PSSR2. The specific 'FSR 4.1 first' interpretation is VGC's analysis, not a standalone Rockstar claim.
articles.why_it_matters: These are useful technical clues for understanding performance and potential PC hardware demands, but they do not establish actual PC system requirements.
articles.verification: VGC coverage of an attributed Rockstar technical statement. Implementation details are not PC benchmarks.

articles.title: No announced PC launch date as console owners begin GTA VI
articles.summary: The Verge discusses the wait facing PC players now that GTA VI is on consoles. Its expectations about eventual Windows hardware optimization are commentary, not an official launch commitment.
articles.why_it_matters: Until Rockstar or Take-Two announces a date, claims about a release window or system requirements should be treated as predictions.
articles.verification: The Verge commentary published November 19; no confirmed PC launch date in the cited official platform release.

articles.title: Digital Foundry finds significant GTA VI frame-rate dips on Xbox Series S
articles.summary: VGC summarizes Digital Foundry tests: Series S targets 30 fps but can spend normal traversal and combat in the mid-20s, with heavy scenes dropping toward 20 fps. The team also praised how much of the game's visual design survives on the lower-power console.
articles.why_it_matters: This is measured console performance, not speculation about a PC port. Future patches could alter the results; the reported measurements apply to the tested launch build.
articles.verification: Independent Digital Foundry tests reported by VGC on November 18, 2026.

articles.title: Digital Foundry: PS5 Pro stays closer to 30 fps than the base PS5
articles.summary: Digital Foundry reports small but noticeable dips under 30 fps on standard PS5. PS5 Pro performed more consistently in their tests, with drops mainly under extreme stress conditions. These are test observations, not guaranteed performance in every situation.
articles.why_it_matters: The comparison helps explain GTA VI's demanding simulation and graphics. It cannot directly predict how a future Windows version or emulator will perform.
articles.verification: VGC's November 18 summary of independent Digital Foundry tests.

articles.title: Netcraft: fake GTA VI and Cyberleek-branded downloads can carry malware
articles.summary: Netcraft documented fraudulent GTA VI downloads, including a fake Cyberleek-branded executable flagged by 34 of 68 security engines. This sample is not established to be Cyberleek's claimed November 23 release.
articles.why_it_matters: Copycat sites are an active malware risk. Safety claims about any newly reported file need a specific hash and independent technical analysis.
articles.verification: Original Netcraft malware research. Distinct copycat download, not independent testing of the promised Xbox executable.
